name: Rate dial knob
oneLiner: a machined aluminium knob on a smoked-glass dial turns with weight from one setting to another, the tick ring and light track follow it, the big readout counts and lands, then up to three knock-on effects pop out with their arrows swinging up or down
say: when the speaker turns one setting up or down and explains what it changes ('raise the rate to 7% and payments go up, savings go down', 'turn the temperature up'): cut in on the setting, the knob lands on the number, the effects pop as they are named. The 9:16 overlay drops the effect chips to stay out of the face zone
